spans.text: ██/██/2064. Lower level of Oberstein's former research facility, White Zone, Frankfurt.
Final Act.
Bam!
Seriously... don't make me do this kind of manual labor, alright? Alright.
Manipulating Tokarev's body, Dandelion smashes through the sealed door with ease. The familiar voice and constant complaints feel utterly out of place coming from Tokarev's face.
The Commander takes a deep breath. Their gun hand is trembling slightly.
Stepping past the shattered doorway, what lies ahead is a vast, hollow laboratory... A frankly tiresome sight for the Commander.
Ever since they became entangled with Paradeus, they have been moving in and out of laboratories and factories like this.
...But all of it ends today.
...Why?
Snap!
In an instant, a blinding red light floods the laboratory, which was previously illuminated only by the dim blue glow of the central machine.
Under this ominous light, the Commander can now clearly make out the massive apparatus... and the man standing before it.
Why is it that you keep showing up again and again...
Like a cockroach that just won't die, buzzing in front of me?
You really can't learn to accept your fate, can you?
Before I ring your death knell? Yes.
Bang!
The Commander fires without hesitation.
But a massive scythe intercepts the bullet before it can reach William, .
Be careful, Commander... This place is pretty "well-stocked".
Dandelion moves slightly closer to the Commander, subtly shielding them.
Before she can even finish, waves of white Nytos emerge like soldiers in formation from both sides of the massive machine, surrounding William at the center.
...Tsk.
Evidently, even with the Lake of Cognition destroyed, he can still control them.
I suppose I should congratulate you—and myself.
After all, witnessing your death first-hand will be quite entertaining for me.
And dying at the hands of these puppets is a most fitting end for you.
The Commander looks up and locks eyes with William across the distance.
Over the past years, Griffin has clashed with him countless times—directly and indirectly, yet never once have they touched the core of his secrets.
And now... in just a few days, they have stood face to face like this multiple times...
With each confrontation taking place under different circumstances, eliciting different feelings.
I've never thought about how I would end up.
Maybe I'd die on the road. Maybe I'd lose everything and become a drifter. Maybe I'd be imprisoned forever, tortured until I become a forgotten skeleton.
I don't care which of those fates would be the most fitting for me.
What becomes of me doesn't matter.
What becomes of YOU... That's what matters.
...What an ardent confession, Commander.
I truly don't understand—why are you so obsessed with me?
Because people like you destroy everything built by those who genuinely try to make this world a better place.
Because people like you feed off the work and sacrifice of others, corrupting the light of idealists.
Because your existence is a disease upon this world.
You have committed evil. You deserve punishment.
...How banal.
Is this your final speech?
Only children cling to a world of good and evil.
I thought you were more mature than that. Seems like I overestimated you.
His face darkens.
I'm tired of this. As you so wish, let's end it here, Commander.
I've already wasted enough time on you.
William raises his hand to issue a command.
But the Nytos before him suddenly freeze, like puppets cut off from their strings, standing completely motionless.
Impressive. Our understanding has reached the point where words are unnecessary.
Thank you for buying me time, Commander. This number was a bit much to handle.
You just called them puppets, didn't you, Little Bill?
How unfortunate. I may not be a puppeteer, but they seem to prefer working with me than with you.
Don't you dare call me that!
Whoosh—
Under Dandelion's control, the white Nytos simultaneously turn their weapons. Their scythes capable of long-range attacks emit beams of white light.
BOOM!!!
The Commander instinctively moves forward, but Dandelion stops them, her expression grave.
...Careful, Commander.
Seems we won't be getting an easy finale after all.
That's...
The explosion and heat from the converging beams has stirred up a dense white haze. By all logic, no human could've survived such an attack.
But there's no mistake.
Within the drifting white smoke, something flutters back and forth...
...A blue butterfly.
...Did you take me for a fool, Commander?
From within the dispersing smoke comes that mocking voice.
The only reason I entertained your pathetic performance... was to see what you were capable of.
What a disappointment.
...Heh.
As the smoke clears, standing beside William atop the platform is—
I have to admit, I thought I had accounted for every possibility.
Yet once again, my perspective proves limited.
Lunasia...?
Hahaha!
That's right, Commander. Look closely.
Watch how your pathetic, filthy lies crumble before the truth.
My sister... never left me.
Through the end of the old world, and the birth of the new—
We will always be together.
You're still so full of mischief... Bill.
But that's alright. Your sister is here. You can indulge yourself.
And it just so happens... I was hoping to personally break that irritating Doll.
There's no one behind me. Are you seeing something we can't? That's unsettling.
...Dandelion.
Relax. I know.
No matter the outcome, this is the last time.
Let us journey to Hell together, Commander.
